root_motivation: Joe (operator) is holding a burst box down until an mcphost branch gate passes. Since 01:05Z none can: `autobuilder vti-plan` exits non-zero on every branch because `.buildloop/ci-equivalent.toml` — added to main by the loop's own push-gate PRD at 00:01Z (commit 4f1112d, the only commit since tag v0.54.1) — matches none of the nine lanes in `agent/proof-lanes.toml`, and vti-plan's `min_confidence` is 0.7. The block is inherited by every branch (gate attribution `inherited=2 in-scope=0`), the reviewer is skipped on the red, and gate-then-land exits 7. Three branches have cycled on it (stdlib-pseudo-modules 01:13Z and 01:57Z, test-suite-consolidation 02:04Z, tenant-self-offboard). The lane file has no test that says "every tracked file routes somewhere", so the gap was found by the gate, after the file was on main, by a different PRD's dispatch.
user_persona: The mcphost build loop's own branch agents and the operator (Joe) supervising them: a branch agent needs `autobuilder vti-plan` to route every path in its diff to a proof lane so its gate measures its own change rather than inheriting main's block, and the operator needs a new unrouted top-level path to be refused at PR time by a named failing test instead of turning every concurrent branch gate red after it lands.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did every mcphost branch gate go red from 01:05Z on 2026-09-16?
five_whys_trace.a: `autobuilder vti-plan` exited non-zero on every branch, and gate attribution read `inherited=2 in-scope=0` -- no branch's own diff was at fault, each was inheriting a block from main.

`.buildloop/ci-equivalent.toml`, added to main at 00:01Z by commit 4f1112d (the only commit since tag v0.54.1), matched none of the nine lanes in agent/proof-lanes.toml, and vti-plan's min_confidence is 0.7, so the unrouted path scored 0.0.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did an unrouted file reach main at all?
five_whys_trace.a: Nothing in the repo asserted that every tracked path routes to some lane, so the only thing that could notice the gap was vti-plan itself -- running after the file had already landed, on a different PRD's branch.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was the gate the only detector?
five_whys_trace.a: proof-lanes.toml is a hand-maintained allowlist with no totality check. Adding a lane alongside a new top-level path was a remembered step, not an enforced one, so it failed the first time someone added a path without thinking about lanes.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a single forgotten line cost the whole repo instead of one PR?
five_whys_trace.a: A lane gap is inherited by every concurrent branch until someone lands a lane, so the cost scales with branch count rather than with the change. The fix is to make totality a CI-time property of the PR that adds the path: a test that walks `git ls-files` and names any path no lane covers, so the lane is added in the same PR.
